title.narrative: Empowering Women & Youth Smallholder Farmers in Groundnut MSD in Abuja, FCT Nigeria.

description.narrative: The project aims to address the socio-economic challenges faced by women and youth smallholder farmers in the FCT by strengthening their participation in the groundnut market system development (MSD). The target communities—Bamishi in Kuje Area Council and Piako in Gwgwalada Area Council of the FCT have significant agricultural potential but are hindered by limited access to resources, market linkages, and technical skills. Many smallholder farmers operate at subsistence levels due to inadequate farming techniques, poor-quality seeds, and a lack of structured market opportunities. This project will provide targeted support to 300 direct beneficiaries (140 women, 60 female youth, 40 male youth, 30 adults male and 30 persons with disabilities) and indirectly impact over 600 community members by equipping them with improved groundnut seeds, training, and post-harvest processing skills to enhance productivity and income. By improving the capacity of farmers, the project will strengthen the MSD by integrating more smallholder farmers into the value chain. Beneficiaries will not only cultivate groundnut for subsistence but will also process and market their products more efficiently. This will create a ripple effect, increasing local supply, reducing post-harvest losses, and ensuring competitive pricing in the marketplace. The formation of cooperatives will further enhance the MSD by creating structured channels for input procurement and market access.
